channel.title: SSM
channel.description: Technical notes by Jaehun Ryu, a deep learning compiler engineer, on LLM inference, KV caches, compilers, C++, AI papers, and open-source code.

item.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
item.description:
Paper

Introduction: The wait before an answer appears

With a long prompt, the model must pass the entire document through before the first token emerges, and the user waits the whole time seeing nothing. To cut that wait, RidgeFill skips computation in some layers and prefills the cache those layers would have produced by approximating it. No training is needed, and the tail, some selected rows, and every decoding step are computed exactly.

item.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
item.description:
Paper

Introduction

As context grows longer, softmax attention’s compute grows quadratically with context length, and the key-value cache grows proportionally to context length. Linear attention, which avoids this, compresses context into a fixed-size matrix memory, but the problem remained that editing that memory disturbs other memories already stored. This paper proposes the Kronecker delta rule, which narrows the scope touched by a single update, and KronLSTM, which implements it as gates.

item.title: GDN Tree-Scan: Served Tree Verification for Recurrent-Hybrid Language Models
item.description:
Paper

LumoTree: Path-Parallel Speculative Verification for Hybrid Language Models

TL;DR — Tree speculative decoding in hybrid models that mix Gated DeltaNet with full attention requires three things to line up on the same “accepted path”: the recurrent state, the convolution history, and the attention KV cache. LumoTree coordinates verification and commit through a single shared tree descriptor, and implements this with a path-parallel scan plus native replay. On an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), it verifies a 27-candidate tree at a cost comparable to a chain stack, and records +7.7%–+11.8% decode throughput over chain MTP. The authors themselves make clear, however, that it does not speed up task completion.

item.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
item.description:
Linear Attention Rewritten with a Kalman Filter: Kalman Delta Networks

TL;DR

The fixed-size recurrent memory update of linear attention is reinterpreted as a linear-Gaussian state-space model, and the covariance tracking of the optimal estimator, the Kalman filter, is introduced to decide “how strongly to overwrite” based on uncertainty, yielding Kalman Delta Networks (KDN). DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, and KDA reduce to fixed-gain special cases that omit the covariance, and KDN outperforms every SOTA linear recurrent mixer evaluated at 750M/1.3B pretraining in both PPL and average accuracy (source: Abstract, §1).

item.title: [Paper Review] Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
item.description:
Paper Link

Marconi: Rethinking Prefix Caching for the Hybrid LLM Era

TL;DR

Marconi introduces a prefix-caching framework for hybrid LLM inference (Attention + SSM).
It selectively admits only highly-reusable prefixes and applies FLOP-per-byte–aware eviction, yielding up to 34.4× higher token-hit rate and 71.1 % lower P95 TTFT (−617 ms) compared with enhanced baselines (vLLM+, SGLang+).
(Evidence: Abstract, Fig. 7–9, § 5.2)

item.title: [Paper Review] Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
item.description:
Paper Link

Structured State Space Duality: Unifying SSMs and Attention with Mamba-2 for 2–8× Acceleration

TL;DR

Structured State-Space Duality (SSD) reveals that SSMs and masked attention compute the same function with different contraction orders. It introduces a matmul-dominant kernel based on block decomposition and low-rank properties, achieving 2–8× speedup over Mamba-scan and outperforming FlashAttention-2 for sequences longer than 2k tokens. In a 2.7B / 300B tokens pre-training setup, it matches the quality of Transformer++ and shows further improvement to a PPL of 5.95 when mixed with 6 attention layers (Source: Abstract, Fig. 10, Tab. 3, §9.2–9.3).
